motivation: In 2007 Lorimer, Bailes, McLaughlin and colleagues found a single, intensely bright, highly dispersed millisecond radio pulse in archival Parkes pulsar-survey data. Its dispersion measure placed it far beyond the Milky Way. This 'Lorimer burst' revealed a new class of cosmic phenomenon: fast radio bursts. Thousands are now known, and they come from extreme compact objects, at least some of them magnetars, as the 2020 Galactic burst from SGR 1935+2154 showed. Because the radio pulses are dispersed by the plasma they cross, FRBs have become precision probes of the intergalactic medium. They have located the cosmic 'missing baryons', they measure magnetic fields along their sight lines, and they offer a new route to cosmological parameters. The discovery came from careful single-pulse search techniques that are now standard, and it set off a worldwide effort to build dedicated instruments. Few results in recent decades have opened so rich a domain of physics.
